subject: Decision criteria, open questions, and demo/test agenda for vendor showdown
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmecorp.com>, Tom Liao <tom.liao@procure.ac>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Decision criteria + proposed test plan (next steps)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so everyone is aligned. I tried to capture the pain points, high-level decision criteria you called out, and a suggested hands-on test plan so Acme can validate each vendor on the same metrics.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Unpredictable token cost and burst latency during peak hours (customer-facing chat).
- Need for private deployment / VPC option for regulated workloads.
- Strong requirement for audit logs and KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Ability to run a throughput/latency head-to-head without changing your existing prompt templates.

Decision criteria (what Acme will evaluate):
1) Latency (p50/p95/p99) at target concurrency and target token lengths
2) Cost per 1M tokens under typical mix (chat + generation)
3) Feasibility of Private deployment + KMS integration timeline
4) Operational visibility: token-level cost breakdown, traceability, and audit logs
5) Model quality on ACME prompt set (we suggested a 20-prompt eval)
6) Fallback behavior / graceful degradation under capacity pressure

Proposed vendor test matrix (attached comparison-matrix.xlsx):
- Standardize on: 50 concurrent users, 1–2k avg context, 75% chat + 25% long generation
- Run: 30-minute sustained run and 5x 1-minute burst tests
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, cost estimate
- Qualitative: 20 prompt QA pass rate (Acme test set) and hallucination checks

Open questions we flagged for Redwood (we'll answer quickly in-line, but listing for the formal record):
- Security: timeline for full Private deployment + KMS proof-of-concept -> We can provision a Private evaluation VPC in ~3–4 weeks with an NDA/SoW; KMS integration depends on keys (we support AWS KMS / GCP KMS / customer HSM).
- Data residency for EU customers -> Redwood has region controls; we can pin inference to eu-west and provide audit logs.
- SLA / credits policy for Dedicated capacity -> I'll loop Marissa for specific contract language.

Immediate next steps (to keep momentum):
1) Acme to confirm the test window (propose Mar 30–31) and share the 20-prompt eval set.
2) Redwood to provision a scoped test environment and provide test harness & scripts (we'll share a lightweight k6 workload + example prompts).
3) Procurement to confirm any additional compliance docs needed (SOC2, ISO certs) — I attached a starter list.

Attachments: comparison-matrix.xlsx (matrix + baseline numbers), redwood-demo-plan.pdf (proposed test scripts + roles)

If that all looks right I can send a calendar invite for the test window and prep doc updates this afternoon.

Best,
Diego
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0122
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmecorp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liao <tom.liao@procure.ac>, procurement@acmecorp.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Decision criteria + proposed test plan (next steps)

Thanks, Diego — this is exactly what we needed; clear and actionable. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Prompt set: we'll share the 20 evaluation prompts by EOD 3/23. They include live-style chat prompts and 5 long generation cases for billing/summary workflows.

2) Competitor coverage: we'll be running Redwood, CloudAI, and InferServe in parallel. Two asks for Redwood specifically:
   - Can you include a short run on KV-cache warm/cold behavior? We saw big p99 variance in prior tests.
   - Can you publish an example of how token-level cost attribution looks in your console (screenshot or short export)?

3) Procurement request: can you provide a draft SOW outline and a sample Dedicated-contract SLA for review so we can scope expected lead times? If you can get the SOW skeleton, that will accelerate our legal review.

Tom will confirm the internal test window, but Mar 30–31 looks good on our preliminary calendar.

Thanks — Sara
Sr. Product Ops, Acme Corp

- I'll export a token-cost attribution sample from the console and drop screenshots into the shared Drive link.

Sara/Tom — once we have the prompts (3/23) and procurement confirmation, I’ll send a calendar invite for the test window (proposed: Mar 30 09:00–17:00 PT & Mar 31 09:00–13:00 PT). If Acme wants us to run the competitor endpoints as well in the same harness we can coordinate that at your direction.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting solid numbers for your evaluation.

Diego
